focus: Pipeline the hot local loops, hit a legal II, and fix false or true recurrences.
merge_rule: Union of gemm_flatten_v1 and flash_no_RMW overlay. On id conflicts, the no-RMW overlay replaces the v1 entry.

skills.pattern: floating-point reduction or accumulation into one scalar inside a loop claimed II=1 (e.g. w -= a*b, sum += expr, acc = acc + expr as the only accumulation chain)
skills.strategy: Do not accumulate into a single scalar inside a pipelined loop. Use private partial accumulators with complete ARRAY_PARTITION, unrolled init/update, then a final tree or serial reduction.
required_steps: detect FP update statements that read and write the same scalar accumulator in the pipelined loop
allocate partial[UF] with complete partition
unroll init and per-lane updates inside pipelined fixed-bound loops
reduce partial[] after the pipelined loop
guards: choose UF to match available DSP/budget
preserve numerics within acceptable reordering for independent partials

skills.pattern: single load task pipelines the outer row loop for multiple large matrices in sequence (matrix A, then B, then C…) each with #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 on the outer i loop
skills.strategy: Split per-matrix load into its own function with innermost pipelined dimension only, or fuse into one flat index loop over all elements. Do not stack multiple outer-pipelined row loops in one task — each outer pipeline asks HLS to move an entire row per cycle and serializes memory ports.
required_steps: detect load functions that outer-pipeline for (i) over rows for more than one large array
remove PIPELINE from outer row loops; pipeline innermost contiguous index (j or flat idx) only
prefer separate load_matrix_A / load_matrix_B helpers or one fused flat load loop
if parallel load tasks are needed, pair each with distinct gmemN bundles and DATAFLOW overlap proof
verify csynth II on hot copy loop — not inflated outer-row pipeline
guards: pair with hls-pipeline-innermost-memory-copy-loop for each matrix
scalar vector loads (b[i]) stay outside inner pipelined j loop
partial final tile uses TILE_SIZE bound + if guards, not runtime tile_size as loop bound

skills.pattern: matrix-vector or dot-product style loops that update an output accumulator array element inside a pipelined and/or unrolled loop (e.g. local_x[i] += expr under #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 or UNROLL over column index j+k)
skills.strategy: Never read-modify-write the same local output accumulator element inside a pipelined unrolled loop. Use private partial accumulators with complete partitioning, reduce once after the pipelined loop, then assign local_x[i] exactly once.
required_steps: detect local_x[i] += or equivalent in-place update inside PIPELINE II=1 or unrolled j+k loops
allocate partial[UF] per output lane or per unroll lane with #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION complete
accumulate into partial[p] inside the pipelined/unrolled loop
reduce partial[] to a scalar after the loop and write local_x[i] once
do not leave loop-carried dependence on local_x[i] in the hot pipeline
guards: applies to local staging buffers as well as m_axi outputs — same RMW discipline
pair with hls-fp-reduction-partial-accumulators for FP dot-product chains
preserve numerical semantics when splitting partial sums

skills.pattern: variable-trip-count loops (triangular, tile_size, k<i, k<j, j=i+1..N) fixed only with LOOP_TRIPCOUNT or LOOP_FLATTEN without rewriting to static bounds
skills.strategy: LOOP_TRIPCOUNT is for reporting/estimation only — it does not make a loop statically bounded, fully unrollable, or dependency-free. Do not rely on LOOP_FLATTEN or LOOP_TRIPCOUNT to legalize pipeline on variable-bound nests.
required_steps: identify loops whose bound depends on an outer induction variable or runtime tile_size
do not add LOOP_TRIPCOUNT as a substitute for static bounds
rewrite to fixed-bound loops with if guards using N or TILE_SIZE constants
re-validate pipeline legality on the rewritten nest
guards: preserve original semantics with if (idx < bound) guards
use header macro constants for fixed bounds

choose an alternative skill that addresses the actual bottleneck

skills.pattern: compute loops perform read-modify-write updates directly on arrays mapped to m_axi ports (e.g. A[i][j] = A[i][j] + expr, x[i] = x[i] + expr, w[i] = w[i] + expr inside nested loops)
skills.strategy: Treat every m_axi argument as external DRAM/HBM. Never read and write the same external element inside an inner loop. Do not use global/m_axi arrays as temporary storage or assume HLS will cache m_axi data across iterations.
required_steps: scan every loop for statements that read and write the same m_axi port element
reject direct accumulation into m_axi arrays
reject repeated reads of the same output element from DRAM/HBM inside an inner loop
reject repeated writes to the same output element inside an inner loop
replace with load-compute-store using local buffers or private scalar accumulators
for reductions, accumulate in a private scalar or local array, then write back once
if the full array is too large, tile/block but still finalize each tile locally before one store
guards: preserve numerical semantics when staging into locals
const read-only m_axi inputs may be read once per tile into locals
in-place outputs still require local write-back buffers, not inner-loop RMW on the port

skills.pattern: memory load/store tile loops with #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 on the outer row/tile loop (for i) while an inner loop iterates all N columns per outer step
skills.strategy: Pipeline the innermost contiguous memory loop only. Do not ask HLS to load or store an entire matrix row per pipeline cycle. Outer i loops should be sequential; inner j loop gets PIPELINE II=1.
required_steps: find load_tile/store_tile nests pipelining the outer i loop
remove PIPELINE from outer loop over tile rows
move PIPELINE II=1 to innermost j loop over contiguous elements
keep scalar row loads (b[i], y[i]) outside or after the inner pipelined j loop
guards: pair with local buffers so inner loop touches BRAM not m_axi when possible
one element per pipeline iteration for m_axi when pipelining global access

skills.pattern: #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 on a parent loop whose body contains another loop that is not fully unrolled (including UNROLL factor=N partial unroll)
skills.strategy: Do not pipeline the parent when a child loop still exists. Partial unroll is not full unroll. Pipeline only the innermost loop, fully unroll the child, or use an explicitly flattenable nest — never assume LOOP_FLATTEN fixes a variable or partially-unrolled child.
required_steps: detect parent PIPELINE pragma with a nested for-loop in the body
check whether every child loop is fully unrolled or the nest is provably flattenable
if any child loop remains, move PIPELINE to innermost legal loop or fully unroll child
do not treat UNROLL factor=4 as removing the child loop
guards: LOOP_FLATTEN does not substitute for full unroll when bounds are variable
validate II on the actual pipelined loop after moving pragmas

skills.pattern: csynth shows L1 / compute_outer / scale outer with Trip=M, II='-', Pipelined=no while a nested L4 / j pipeline reports II=1 — including syr2k/syrk form L1{ L2; L3{ L4 PIPELINE } } where per-i cost ≈ L2 + K*N and total ≈ M*(L2+K*N)
skills.strategy: Treat as a latency bug. Do not stop after L4 II=1. Apply hls-gemm-static-nest-flatten-and-k-partition or hls-syr2k-triangle-flatten-k-unroll: fixed j bounds + if guards, (i,j) PIPELINE+FLATTEN, k UNROLL, matching ARRAY_PARTITION. Re-synth until L1 is no longer an unpipelined trip=M loop dominating latency. After flatten+k-unroll, if Final II ≫ 1 from a serial FP accumulator, continue with hls-avoid-serial-fp-acc-under-full-k-unroll — do not stop.
required_steps: detect outer L1/compute with Pipelined=no and II=- next to an II=1 inner j/L4 pipeline
do not accept the design as optimized
for syr2k/syrk also reject for (j=0;j<=i) variable bounds — rewrite to j<N + if (j<=i)
route to hls-syr2k-triangle-flatten-k-unroll / hls-gemm-static-nest-flatten-and-k-partition
re-synth and confirm outer sequential L1 is gone or no longer dominates (flattened (i,j) trip)
if flattened region still has Final II ≫ 1 from serial FP reduction, route to hls-avoid-serial-fp-acc-under-full-k-unroll
guards: applies to static-bound full-workspace or within-tile GEMM nests, not irreducible true dependencies
staging only inputs but leaving outputs or accumulators on global memory is incomplete
reading one operand from global inside a pipelined compute loop usually destroys II and bandwidth
skills.pattern: some inputs are loaded into local buffers, but the hot compute loop still reads or writes one or more m_axi array parameters directly, such as an accumulator matrix, temporary, or output array
required_steps: list every array indexed inside each pipelined compute loop
if any index targets a function parameter array, stage that array locally or privatize the accessed region
route to hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate or hls-chain-intermediate-results-locally
validate that compute loops reference only local buffers
skills.strategy: do not mix local staging with global reads or writes in the same hot compute loop; stage all operands and outputs used in compute locally first

skills.pattern: optimization stops because the innermost feasible loop achieved II=1, while total module latency is still dominated by a sequential outer trip over rows/columns of a static GEMM
skills.strategy: II on one loop is not the objective — total cycles are. For static GEMM and syr2k/syrk nests, require flatten of the (i,j) nest (with k unrolled) and validate against top latency / L1 table, not only Final II=1 on L4/j. Use hls-syr2k-triangle-flatten-k-unroll for triangular updates Total cycles require both flatten and low achieved II on the flattened region (reject serial-FP-acc II blowups via hls-avoid-serial-fp-acc-under-full-k-unroll).
required_steps: after any PIPELINE success on an inner loop, read the parent loop table
if parent is unpipelined with large trip count, continue with flatten+partition repairs
compare sibling phases and fix any phase that did not flatten
guards: still prefer innermost pipeline for non-flattenable or true-recurrence cases
PIPELINE is a scheduling request, not proof that the schedule improved
pragma-only changes should be rejected when the report bottleneck remains unchanged
skills.pattern: a proposed pipeline transformation only adds a PIPELINE pragma but does not address the reported reason why II is high or scheduling is blocked
required_steps: check achieved II, not only requested II
read scheduling warnings and dependency reports
resolve memory ports, false dependencies, AXI access, recurrences, or body latency as appropriate
do not claim success if the report still shows the same II bottleneck
skills.strategy: do not treat PIPELINE pragma insertion as complete unless achieved II or latency improves, or the actual scheduling bottleneck is addressed

guards: avoid-tier skills must not cause fallback to unoptimized reference code
when in doubt, apply hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate rather than emitting textbook C
skills.pattern: the model avoids advanced transforms because of many avoid rules or uncertainty, and responds with textbook nested loops on global arrays and no compute pragmas
required_steps: detect reference-port output despite loaded skill catalog
do not treat caution as permission to skip optimization
apply hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate, hls-multi-phase-local-pipeline, or hls-iterative-stencil-timestep-local-volume as appropriate
ensure PIPELINE pragmas exist before submitting
skills.strategy: avoid rules forbid unsafe transforms, not all transforms; when uncertain, still apply the baseline local load-compute-store recipe instead of reference C

guards: m_axi interface pragmas alone do not constitute optimization
absence of PIPELINE, local buffers, or loop restructuring on a memory-bound hot loop is a blocking defect
skills.pattern: proposed or current code performs the main computation by directly indexing m_axi or global array parameters with no local staging and no HLS pragmas on the hot loops, including multi-phase kernels with many m_axi ports
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate or hls-multi-phase-local-pipeline before any other optimization

skills.pattern: static-bound GEMM/matmul (or 2mm/3mm phase) on locals with PIPELINE on (i,j) (often + LOOP_FLATTEN) and full UNROLL on reduction k, but csynth Final II remains huge (tens–hundreds) because a single float/double accumulator carries a true FP dependence and/or dmul/dadd are resource-shared down to ~1 instance — so latency ≈ trip×II stays catastrophic despite 'k fully unrolled'
skills.strategy: Do not treat full k UNROLL or outer flatten as success when achieved II ≫ 1. Rewrite the reduction with lane/partial sums or a tree (hls-unroll-reduction-partial-sums / ii-reduction-lane-partial-tree), allocate enough FP operators for the chosen parallelism, or fall back to pipeline-on-k with modest outer/j unroll (ChatHLS-style). Re-synth until Final II is near the legal target.
required_steps: detect full k UNROLL under (i,j) pipeline with serial sum += a*b (float/double)
read csynth Final II, accumulator dependence, and dmul/dadd binding/sharing
if Final II ≫ 1 from FP reduction or resource limit, reject the design as optimized
route to partial-sum/tree reduction + matching resources, or pipeline-on-k fallback
re-synth and confirm Final II improved; do not stop at flatten-only success
guards: still prefer flatten of sequential outer i when that is the bug (hls-avoid-outer-sequential-gemm-after-inner-pipeline)
preserve numerical tolerance expectations when reassociating FP reductions
device util ≤ 100% after allocating more operators / wider trees
m_axi interface pragmas alone are not an optimized kernel
a flash output with only interface pragmas will synthesize as unpipelined scalar hardware
uncertainty about advanced optimizations does not justify skipping the baseline gate
skills.pattern: the proposed kernel body has no #pragma HLS PIPELINE on any compute loop, or the only pragmas are m_axi or s_axilite interface pragmas
required_steps: scan the kernel body for #pragma HLS PIPELINE on compute loops
if none are present, reject the output as a reference port
route to hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate and hls-multi-phase-local-pipeline
add pipelined load, local compute, and store loops before resubmitting
skills.strategy: never submit a kernel whose hot loops lack PIPELINE pragmas; apply the baseline load-compute-store gate first even when avoid rules discourage advanced transforms

guards: false-dependence pragmas can silently produce incorrect hardware when applied to true hazards
do not prioritize II=1 over semantic correctness
if exact sequential order is required, algorithmic restructuring may not be legal
skills.pattern: a proposed fix uses DEPENDENCE inter false on an array or accumulator that is truly read and written across iterations, such as a reduction, histogram, in-place update, or same-address read-modify-write
required_steps: check whether two iterations can access the same location with at least one write
classify the dependence as reduction, scatter/RMW, stencil/in-place update, or inherent recurrence
route to partial accumulators, privatization, old/new buffering, wavefront, or best-legal-II handling
remove unsafe false-dependence pragma proposals
validate correctness before measuring II
skills.strategy: reject the false-dependence pragma and use a legal transformation instead: partial sums for reductions, privatized accumulators for RMW/scatter, old/new buffers for Jacobi-style updates, or accept the legal II for inherently serial recurrences
